title: Toxic Feeds: Mapping the Digital Harms Ecosystem, Escalation and Accountability in Somalia
content: Somalia’s digital information environment has expanded faster than the institutions, norms, and laws needed to manage it. The country had 10.7 million internet users at the start of 2025, equivalent to 55.2 percent internet penetration, and 3.05 million social media user identities. Public platform figures should be interpreted carefully because advertising reach, registered identities, shared devices and actual users are not the same measure. Connectivity has created real benefits: civic voices can reach national audiences, diaspora communities remain closely connected to local debates, mobile money underpins everyday transactions, and remote education and information-sharing are more accessible than in previous decades. Yet the same infrastructure is also used to manufacture narratives, weaponise clan identity, silence women, intimidate journalists and accelerate conflict dynamics.
